question: How do we check whether a shuttle has the right speed?

answer.reasoning: The question has one part: how to check whether a shuttle has the right speed (i.e., the sources do not say how to check whether a shuttle has the right speed). Law 3.1 sentences (1) and (2) give the testing method — a full underhand stroke contacting the shuttle over the back boundary line, hit at an upward angle parallel to the side lines — and Law 3.2 sentence (1) gives the pass criterion: a shuttle of correct speed lands not less than 530 mm and not more than 990 mm short of the other back boundary line as in Diagram B. These three sentences together answer the part. Related but non-answering sentences: Diagram B itself (laws-Diagram B (1)), the ITTO guidance on who should test (itto-3.5.4.1 (1)), on assessing the manner of the hit (itto-3.5.4.4 (1)), and the Referee re-checking speed during play (itto-3.6.3 (1)).
answer.answer: To check whether a shuttle has the right speed, a player shall use a full underhand stroke which makes contact with the shuttle over the back boundary line [1], hit the shuttle at an upward angle and in a direction parallel to the side lines [2], and a shuttle of correct speed will land not less than 530 mm and not more than 990 mm short of the other back boundary line as in Diagram B [3]. The shuttles should be tested by an active player in the tournament, preferably a male player, or a qualified person approved by the Referee [4]. When assessing the result of the shuttle test, take into account the manner in which the shuttles were hit, including the strength of shot and trajectory, and whether they were hit from the correct location over the back line [5]. The Referee shall at all times, when observing play, consider whether the shuttle speed selected before play started still appears to be correct [6].

citations.quote: To test a shuttle, a player shall use a full underhand stroke which makes contact with the shuttle over the back boundary line.
The shuttle shall be hit at an upward angle and in a direction parallel to the side lines.
A shuttle of correct speed will land not less than 530 mm and not more than 990 mm short of the other back boundary line as in Diagram B.
The shuttles should be tested by an active player in the tournament, preferably a male player, or a qualified person approved by the Referee.

question: In doubles, in what order does the right to serve pass?

No search is needed. Law 11.6 (who serves first in the next game) bears on serving order but does not answer the in-game sequence, so it goes in related_sentences.

Either player of the winning side may serve first in the next game, and either player of the losing side may receive first in the next game [7].

answer.answer: A player is entitled to a minimum 60-minute interval between two matches, and in exceptional circumstances the Referee can reduce that interval to no less than 30 minutes [1]. question: What does a black card mean, and who decides to give it?

answer.reasoning: The question has two parts: (1) what a black card means, and (2) who decides to give it. Part 1 is answered by itto-5.17.5: sentence (1) states a black card is given when the Referee decides to disqualify, and sentences (3) and (4) state the Umpire announces "disqualified for misconduct" while raising the black card — so the black card signals disqualification for misconduct. Part 2 is answered by itto-5.17.5 sentence (1) ("When the Referee decides to disqualify...") and laws-16.7.2 sentence (1) ("the Referee, who shall have the power to disqualify the offending side from the match"). Both parts are fully answered by the given sources, so no search is needed. Related: itto-5.17.10 (2) notes cards given before the match have no effect on the score, and itto-3.6.2 (1) covers when the Referee is called for flagrant misbehaviour, but these do not answer either part directly.
answer.answer: A black card means that the offending player or pair is disqualified for misconduct, and the Referee decides to give it, with the card being given to the Umpire [1]. When the Referee decides to disqualify, the Umpire calls "Come here" to the offending player or pair, announces the player's name followed by "disqualified for misconduct" and a specific explanation of the misconduct, and at the same time raises the right hand holding the black card above the Umpire's head [2][3]. The Referee has the power to disqualify the offending side from the match after the umpire reports the offending side immediately [4]. Any card given has no effect on the score of the match, but it is taken into account if further offences occur during the match [5].
